speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific movements you've been experiencing, and when did they first start? Also, what psychiatric symptoms or medications were you dealing with before these movements began?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: I'm glad to hear your psychiatric symptoms have improved, but I need to understand the movement issue better. Can you describe exactly what these new movements look like, and have you noticed any muscle stiffness or restlessness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: This sounds like akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. Do you have any muscle stiffness, slow movements, or tremors that might suggest other movement issues? Has this restlessness made you feel anxious or want to stop taking your medication?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your clear description of restlessness and fidgeting starting after beginning risperidone, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Risperidone-induced Akathisia.
